an1.67:1.1: “Rational application of mind” (_yoniso manasikāra_) is a distinctively Buddhist term. It draws on the frequent Vedic image of the “womb of truth” (_yonāv ṛtasya_, Rig Veda 9.13.9), the source of the laws and patterns that govern the natural order. The idea is that by applying the mind by way of cause or reason the hidden truth can be uncovered. Here the meditator’s insight is framed not as uncovering the objective truth about the world, but as reflexively understanding the means of insight itself.
an1.68:1.1: “Situational awareness” is a psychological term popularized in the 1990s. It has to do with the perception of environmental phenomena and the comprehension of their meaning, which is very close to the sense of the Pali term _sampajañña_. It is applied broadly, for example, to telling a deliberate lie ([an3.28:1.5]()), awareness of activities ([an4.198:12.1]()), awareness of mental phenomena as they rise and pass ([an4.41:4.2]()), and to the mind in absorption ([an4.163:4.4]()).
